lead.title: A fortune held in code now belongs to 135,694 people, and the households it is starting to build run on different assumptions
lead.standfirst: Henley & Partners counts 290 crypto centi millionaires and 23 crypto billionaires, a cohort that is younger, more mobile and more secretive than the wealth private service was built around.
lead.body:
The Crypto Wealth Report 2026, published by Henley & Partners on 8 September, puts 135,694 individuals in possession of at least USD 1 million in digital assets. Of those, 92,272 hold that million in Bitcoin alone. Above them sit 290 centi millionaires with USD 100 million or more, 151 of them in Bitcoin, and 23 billionaires, of whom nine are Bitcoin billionaires. The total market stood at USD 2.6 trillion as at 31 August 2026, USD 1.6 trillion of it in Bitcoin.

The striking figure is the base beneath the pyramid. Some 742 million people now hold digital assets in some quantity, 371 million of them holding Bitcoin, and that number kept widening through a year in which the market itself contracted from its record highs. Singapore tops the report's Crypto Adoption Index for the fourth consecutive year, which matters less as a league table than as a signal of where this cohort chooses to keep a residence, a company and a banking relationship.

This is a small population by the standards of the wealth reports this Journal usually reads. Altrata counts more than half a million ultra wealthy individuals worldwide. A hundred and thirty five thousand crypto millionaires is a fraction of that, and a fortune in digital assets is rarely the whole of anyone's balance sheet. What makes the cohort worth understanding is its shape rather than its size. It skews young, it is unusually mobile, it is concentrated in a handful of jurisdictions, and it has been formed by an asset class where the loss of a credential is the loss of the asset itself.

That last point is the one that reaches the house. In a family whose wealth sits in property, art and securities, the custodians are banks, registrars and insurers, and a mistake by a member of staff is embarrassing rather than terminal. In a household where a material part of the fortune is a private key, the perimeter includes the study, the safe, the devices left charging in a kitchen and the person who answers the door to the engineer who has come to look at the network. The principal may be thirty two. The standards will be no softer for it.
lead.why: A new cohort of principals is forming, and it is young, mobile and unusually exposed to failures of physical and digital security. Household staff who understand device discipline, visitor control and the handling of anything that looks like a credential will be valuable to them in a way that polish alone is not.

articles.title: Confidentiality has become a line in the salary, and in Los Angeles it is written into three quarters of assistant contracts
articles.body:
Morgan & Mallet International's Household Staff Annual Report 2025/26, drawn from a database of more than 50,300 candidates and covering 28 positions across eight markets, states the matter plainly. Privacy adds 15 to 20 per cent to a salary. Candidates who can demonstrate discretion, rather than merely promise it, are placed at 10 to 15 per cent above market rates for the same role.

The clearest evidence sits in Los Angeles, where 77 per cent of personal assistant placements now require a signed non disclosure agreement. The agreement is not the point. What the figure describes is a market in which a household's exposure is assumed rather than argued about, and in which the assistant is treated as part of the family's risk management rather than as its diary keeper. In Miami, 79 per cent of placed assistants have already worked alongside a security team. In Manhattan, 91 per cent handle private school applications, a file that contains almost everything a family would least like to see circulated.

The money follows. American personal assistants are placed from USD 80,000 to USD 250,000, and executive assistants from USD 120,000 to USD 250,000, the widest band of any role in the report outside the chief of staff. The spread is not explained by typing speed. It is explained by what a family is prepared to hand over, and to whom.

Retention tells the same story from the other side. Ninety two per cent of assistants placed in Los Angeles stay two years or longer, in a sector where average tenure across all roles has collapsed to roughly three years. Eighty four per cent have worked for families worth USD 30 million or more. Households that have found someone they trust are visibly unwilling to repeat the exercise, and they pay to avoid it.

For a candidate entering the profession, this is the most actionable finding in the report. Language, cuisine and service technique can be taught in months. A verifiable record of confidentiality takes years and cannot be bought, which is exactly why it commands a premium that no qualification does.
articles.why: Discretion is the one part of the craft that is both priced explicitly and impossible to acquire quickly. A candidate who can point to years of confidential work, and to referees willing to confirm it, is negotiating from a different position than one who cannot.
articles.src: Morgan & Mallet International, Household Staff Annual Report 2025/26

articles.title: The supply of twin engine helicopters has fallen by a third in six months, and the family that wants one will be waiting
articles.body:
AeroAsset's twin engine helicopter report for the first half of 2026 records retail transactions up 8 per cent year on year while the number of aircraft available for sale fell 33 per cent. Sixty seven machines changed hands against only 123 left on the global market. The absorption rate has tightened to roughly 11 months, which is to say that at the current pace the entire world inventory of second hand twins would clear before next August.

The squeeze is not evenly spread. Light twins saw volume slip 4 per cent while inventory fell 44 per cent. Medium twins posted the strongest growth of any high volume category at 38 per cent, and their supply is now at a five year low. Heavy twins sold two more units than last year on supply down 10 per cent. North America accounted for 46 per cent of transactions and Europe for 31 per cent, with European volumes up 75 per cent year on year, while Asia Pacific fell 42 per cent and Latin America 47 per cent.

Liquidity, in this market, is a practical matter rather than an abstraction. The Airbus H135 and H145 families trade most readily, followed by the Leonardo AW109S and SP, the Bell 429 and the Sikorsky S-76C+ and C++. The Airbus H155 and the Sikorsky S-76D are the hardest to move. A family asking to buy the machine it already likes may find the answer is a two year wait or a different type.

None of this is remote from the house. The twin engine helicopter is the aircraft that connects an estate to an airport, a Mediterranean villa to a marina and a Swiss chalet to a valley floor in February. It is flown with two engines precisely because it carries principals over water and over cities. When the supply of those machines halves, the schedule that depends on them becomes less forgiving, charter rates firm, and the person building the family's diary has less margin for error than the year before.
articles.why: Estate and house managers increasingly coordinate rotary transfers as a matter of routine. A tightening market means fewer aircraft available at short notice, firmer charter pricing and longer lead times, all of which land on whoever holds the schedule.

articles.title: Seventeen of the twenty five most expensive wines in the world now come from two Burgundy domaines held by the same owner
articles.body:
WineCap's ranking of the most expensive fine wine brands of 2026, reported at the start of September, places Domaine de la Romanee-Conti at the summit at GBP 195,406 a case. Immediately behind it sits d'Auvenay's Chevalier-Montrachet Grand Cru at GBP 186,419 a case of twelve. What the list reveals, however, is concentration rather than hierarchy. Of the twenty five names, seventeen belong to just two houses, Domaine Leroy with eleven entries and Domaine d'Auvenay with six.

Both are the property of Lalou Bize-Leroy, who also retains a quarter share of Domaine de la Romanee-Conti. Together the two domaines account for 64.1 per cent of the ranking's combined value. The explanation is scarcity carried to an extreme. D'Auvenay farms 3.87 hectares spread across sixteen appellations, and its holding in Criots-Batard-Montrachet extends to 0.064 hectares, a parcel that yields a few hundred bottles in a good year.

White Burgundy is disproportionately represented at the very top, taking three of the four most expensive wines and five of the top ten, with an average case price of GBP 102,197 against GBP 74,822 for red. Only one wine in the top twenty five comes from outside Burgundy at all: Chave's Ermitage Cathelin, in fifteenth place at GBP 61,143. Screaming Eagle Sauvignon Blanc follows in twenty eighth, Petrus is the highest Bordeaux at forty sixth, Krug Clos du Mesnil the highest Champagne at eightieth and Soldera Case Basse the highest Italian at ninety ninth.

Prices at this altitude are not rising. Seventeen of the top twenty five declined by an average of 2.0 per cent over the last twelve months, and Romanee-Conti, for all its position, delivered the weakest ten year appreciation in the group at 70.9 per cent. The market has corrected since its 2022 peak and these bottles corrected with it.

For a household, the practical reading is about custody rather than investment. A cellar that contains any of these names holds objects whose value rests on provenance, condition and an unbroken record of storage. A single warm summer in a badly regulated room, or a case moved between houses without documentation, erases more value than most people imagine is at stake in a wine rack.
articles.why: Cellar management is a standard part of a senior household brief. Knowing which names carry this kind of value, and that their worth depends on temperature records and provenance rather than labels alone, is the difference between storing wine and looking after an asset.
articles.src: WineCap, reported by The Drinks Business

briefs.b: GlobalAir.com's marketplace snapshot of 1 September 2026 shows large cabin jets clearing fastest of any turbine class, at a median 79 days on the market against 6.5 months of supply. Midsize jets sit 131 days on 8.0 months, and twin turboprops 159 days. AMSTAT reports median heavy jet transaction values up 13 per cent year on year with only 5.2 per cent of that fleet listed for sale.

Frieze London and Frieze Masters return to The Regent's Park from 14 to 18 October. The invitation only preview falls on Wednesday 14 October, with general admission from the 15th. Tickets are date and time specific and sold online only, with no admission at the gate, so a principal's attendance has to be arranged well in advance.

Twenty two per cent of clients ask specifically for a traditional English butler holding certification from a recognised school, according to Morgan & Mallet. Butlers make up about 5 per cent of the agency's registered profiles, average seven years of experience and are placed at a 96 per cent success rate. Nine per cent of butlers worldwide are women. The highest placed salary, in the United States, reaches USD 180,000.
